messages.subject: Simply "echo"/parse a source file?
parts:
Hi

My request is quite simple, but I am not sure how I should do this: I
simply want to show in the pdf the R code used (say file.R), without
even the need to evaluate the file.

The solution I found is to use something like:
srcref(srcfile(filename=file.R), lloc=c(1,1,10000,10000))

but the code is reported as "output of R function", and hence appears
with ## instead of being highlighted as input. How can I tel knitr to
"show as input the output of the R function"?

Thanks!

Mat

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Simply "echo"/parse a source file?
parts:
Great question, and you can do it with the development version of
knitr on Github.

library(devtools); install_github('knitr', 'yihui')

The read_chunk() function allows you to read external R code and
insert it into a document; in your case, you only need

<<read-code, include=FALSE>>=
read_chunk('file.R', labels='foobar') # need to specify a label for reference
@
% then insert the code to a chunk
<<foobar, eval=FALSE>>=
@

You can have finer control of the code in file.R, e.g. you can put the
first 10 lines into one chunk, and line 23-47 to another, etc. See
?read_chunk

Regards,
Yihui
